stories.summary: A new study finds that simply increasing a multimodal model's inference budget gives only modest gains on 22 visual-reasoning benchmarks, arguing agents instead need external tools for grounded perception and measurement.

They found that boosting a base multimodal model's inference budget alone produced only modest improvements. Many tasks instead require grounded perception, external knowledge, and numerical measurements that come from heterogeneous external tools. stories.title: Paper argues coding agents need harness and policy to evolve together
stories.summary: Researchers argue that an LLM coding agent's performance depends jointly on its policy model and the harness mediating its environment, and that evolving only one of the two is suboptimal.
stories.more: LLM coding agents' performance is jointly determined by the policy model and the harness that mediates how it interacts with its environment, the authors argue. A harness tuned for one model checkpoint may miss the failure modes of an updated policy, while policy learning stays limited to trajectories the fixed harness happens to elicit. The paper's premise is that harness and policy are mutually reinforcing, so evolving only one is suboptimal. The excerpt ends before describing the proposed method for co-evolving both.

stories.summary: A new technique called MT Forcing addresses drift in multi-turn image editing, where existing methods accumulate visual artifacts and make unintended changes to preserved regions after just a few edits.
stories.more: Multi-turn image editing lets users modify an image through a sequence of instructions, meant to make interactive visual content creation easier. Existing methods, the authors say, drift noticeably after only a few editing turns. This drift shows up two ways: visual quality degrades with accumulating artifacts, and image content becomes inconsistent as unintended changes creep into regions and edits that should have been preserved. The excerpt cuts off just as it introduces the proposed fix, MT Forcing, so its mechanism isn't described.

stories.title: RoAR-VAE simplifies tokenizer training while keeping diffusion performance
stories.summary: Revisiting the REPA-E tokenizer approach, researchers find that dropping its diffusion objective and generative blocks while keeping semantic prediction from corrupted latents matches downstream diffusion performance.
stories.more: A good visual tokenizer needs to preserve image fidelity while producing latents that downstream diffusion models can learn from efficiently. Prior methods improved this latent diffusability through semantic alignment or by training the tokenizer and diffusion model jointly. The authors revisit REPA-E, one such approach, and find that removing its diffusion objective and dedicated generative blocks has little cost: keeping only semantic prediction from corrupted latents yields comparable downstream generation performance under a matched setup. The excerpt is cut off before further results.
